symbols.name: P
symbols.role: generic row law used as an argument of the empirical recursion

symbols.name: h
symbols.role: direction for differentiation of a row-law functional

symbols.name: P_N
symbols.role: law of the size-\(N\) observed array

symbols.name: \underline\kappa
symbols.role: uniform lower bound for retained Gram eigenvalues

symbols.name: \underline\rho
symbols.role: uniform lower bound for every residual pivot at which a square-root derivative is evaluated

symbols.name: P_{0X}
symbols.role: joint law of the initial outcome and covariate

symbols.name: G_{ij}
symbols.role: entry of the one latent matrix reused at every date

symbols.name: Z_{it}^{\circ}
symbols.def: independent \(\mathcal N(0,1)\) variables independent of the initial rows, assignments, and outcome innovations

symbols.name: \mathcal U_{\mathrm{rr}}
symbols.def: the open row-law class in \(\text{def:rank-regular-domain}\) on which every full past-message Gram block has margin \(\underline\kappa\) and every Schur residual has margin \(\underline\rho\)

symbols.name: H_{it}
symbols.def: With \(D_0^{\star}=\varnothing\), \(H_{i,D_0^{\star}}=0\), and \(\lambda_0=0\), set \(H_{it}=\lambda_t^{\top}H_{i,D_t^{\star}}+\sqrt{\rho_t}Z_{it}^{\circ}\) for every \(0\le t<T\).

symbols.name: \mathscr F_{N,t}
symbols.def: \(\mathscr F_{N,t}=\sigma\{(Y_{i0},X_i,W_{i,1:T},\epsilon_{i,0:T-1})_{i=1}^N,(\mathbf U_s)_{0\le s\le t},(H_{is}^{G,N})_{1\le i\le N,0\le s<t}\}\)

symbols.name: \mathcal A_{N,t}^{\mathrm{act}}
symbols.def: the \(\mathscr F_{N,t}\)-measurable event on which \(\lambda_t^{N}\) is defined and \(\rho_t^{N}>0\), with the inverse condition omitted at \(t=0\)

symbols.name: H_{it}^{\circ,N}
symbols.def: recursively, \(H_{it}^{\circ,N}=(\lambda_t^{N})^{\top}H_{i,D_t^{\star}}^{\circ,N}+\sqrt{\rho_t^{N}}Z_{it}^{\circ}\), starting from the empty past at \(t=0\)

symbols.name: \mathfrak R_T(P)
symbols.def: for \(P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{rr}}\), start at \(Y_0,X,W,\epsilon,Z^{\circ}\); recursively set \(U_t=g_{\beta_0}(Y_t,W_{t+1},X)\), \(K_{rs}(P)=P[U_rU_s]\), use the full past set \(D_t^{\star}=\{0,\ldots,t-1\}\), form \(\lambda_t(P)\) and \(\rho_t(P)\), set \(H_t=\lambda_t(P)^{\top}H_{D_t^{\star}}+\sqrt{\rho_t(P)}Z_t^{\circ}\), and \(Y_{t+1}=P[U_t]+\sqrt{\sigma^2}H_t+\epsilon_t\)

symbols.name: M_N
symbols.def: on \(\{\mathbb P_N\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{rr}}\}\), \(M_N=\mathfrak M_T(\mathbb P_N)\) from the full-rank recursion, ordered as outcome means, message means, centered outcome variances, upper-triangular message Gram products, mean-score Jacobians, and variance-score Jacobians; set \(M_N=0\) on the complementary event

symbols.name: \dot{\mathfrak R}_T[h]
symbols.def: for \(P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{rr}}\) and any ambient empirical-process direction \(h\) with \(h[1]=0\), the recursion obtained from \(\mathfrak R_T(P)\) by the ordinary product and chain rules on \(D_t^{\star}=\{0,\ldots,t-1\}\), with \(\dot\mu_t[h]=h[U_t]+P[\dot U_t[h]]\), \(\dot K_{rs}[h]=h[U_rU_s]+P[\dot U_r[h]U_s+U_r\dot U_s[h]]\), \(\dot\lambda_t[h]=K_{D_t^{\star}D_t^{\star}}^{-1}\{\dot K_{D_t^{\star},t}[h]-\dot K_{D_t^{\star}D_t^{\star}}[h]\lambda_t\}\), \(\dot\rho_t[h]=\dot K_{tt}[h]-2\dot K_{t,D_t^{\star}}[h]\lambda_t+\lambda_t^{\top}\dot K_{D_t^{\star}D_t^{\star}}[h]\lambda_t\), and \(\dot H_t[h]=\dot\lambda_t[h]^{\top}H_{D_t^{\star}}+\lambda_t^{\top}\dot H_{D_t^{\star}}[h]+\dot\rho_t[h]Z_t^{\circ}/(2\sqrt{\rho_t})\). Finally, \(\dot Y_{t+1}[h]=\dot\mu_t[h]+\sqrt{\sigma^2}\dot H_t[h]\).

symbols.name: \dot\phi_T(\xi;P)[h]
symbols.type: directional derivative of the ordered feature vector
symbols.def: the coordinatewise product-rule derivative of the displayed vector \(\phi_T(\xi;P)\), with every outcome and message derivative supplied by \(\dot{\mathfrak R}_T[h]\)

symbols.name: \mathcal F_{0X,T}
symbols.def: a fixed finite collection of square-integrable functions of \(Y_0,X\) containing the initial-row coordinate integrands and every propagated first-derivative integrand required by the \(T\)-step counterfactual path

symbols.name: \mathbb Z_T^{\mathrm{full}}
symbols.def: \(\mathbb Z_T^{\mathrm{full}}(b,f)\) is the centered Gaussian process indexed by \(b\in\mathbb R^{\dim(M_T)}\) and \(f\in\mathcal F_{0X,T}\), with \[\operatorname{Cov}\{\mathbb Z_T^{\mathrm{full}}(b,f),\mathbb Z_T^{\mathrm{full}}(c,g)\}=P_\xi[(b^{\top}I_T(\xi)+f(Y_0,X)-P_{0X}f)(c^{\top}I_T(\xi)+g(Y_0,X)-P_{0X}g)].\] Thus the displayed covariance specifies the moment block, initial empirical-process block, and every cross-block covariance through the same CFSE influence recursion.

symbols.name: Z_M
symbols.def: the centered Gaussian vector characterized by \(b^{\top}Z_M=\mathbb Z_T^{\mathrm{full}}(b,0)\)

symbols.name: S_m
symbols.def: the fixed linear map from the ordered moment coordinates in \(M_T\) that subtracts message means from next-outcome means

symbols.name: S_v
symbols.def: the fixed linear map from the ordered moment coordinates in \(M_T\) that subtracts \(\sigma^2\) times the message-energy coordinates from the centered next-outcome-variance coordinates

symbols.name: Z_{mv}
symbols.def: \(Z_{mv}=(Z_m^{\top},Z_v^{\top})^{\top}\sim\mathcal N(0,\operatorname{blockdiag}\{C,2(C\circ C)\})\), as the residual projection of \(\mathbb Z_T^{\mathrm{full}}\)

symbols.name: \widehat\sigma^2
symbols.def: the first coordinate of \((\widehat X_v^{\top}W_v\widehat X_v)^{-1}\widehat X_v^{\top}W_v\widehat v\)

symbols.name: \widehat\tau^2
symbols.def: the second coordinate of \((\widehat X_v^{\top}W_v\widehat X_v)^{-1}\widehat X_v^{\top}W_v\widehat v\)

symbols.name: \widehat\zeta_i
symbols.def: write \(\bar e=N^{-1}\sum_j\widehat e_j\), \(\widehat z_{m,i}=\widehat e_i-\bar e\), and \(\widehat z_{v,i}=\widehat e_i\circ\widehat e_i-N^{-1}\sum_j\widehat e_j\circ\widehat e_j\); then \(\widehat\zeta_i=(\widehat L\widehat z_{m,i},\widehat A_v\{\widehat z_{v,i}-\widehat\sigma^2\widehat Q_\beta\widehat L\widehat z_{m,i}\},\delta_{(Y_{i0},X_i)}-\widehat P_{0X})\)

symbols.name: \widehat\psi_{\theta,T,i}
symbols.def: \(\widehat\psi_{\theta,T,i}=D\Psi_T(\widehat\beta,\widehat\sigma^2,\widehat\tau^2,\widehat P_{0X})[\widehat\zeta_i]\), where the derivative is evaluated by forward differentiation of every displayed scalar update in \(\Psi_T\)

symbols.name: c_{1-\alpha}
symbols.def: the conditional \(1-\alpha\) quantile of \(\max_{1\le t\le T}|Z_t^\theta|\)

symbols.name: \mathcal C_N
symbols.def: \(\mathcal C_{N,t}=[\widehat\theta_{T,t}-c_{1-\alpha}/\sqrt N,\widehat\theta_{T,t}+c_{1-\alpha}/\sqrt N]\) for every \(1\le t\le T\)

symbols.name: Q
symbols.role: index collecting a primitive-row law and the finite-dimensional homogeneous Causal-MP parameters for the fixed horizon

symbols.name: P_{0X,Q}
symbols.type: initial-row law induced by a model index
symbols.role: the initial-outcome and covariate component of Q

symbols.name: \beta_{0,Q}
symbols.type: structural parameter at model index Q

symbols.name: \sigma_Q^2
symbols.type: interaction variance at model index Q

symbols.name: \tau_Q^2
symbols.type: innovation variance at model index Q

symbols.name: p_{t,Q}
symbols.type: assignment probability at model index Q

symbols.name: P_{\xi,Q}
symbols.def: the product law of \(\xi_i\) obtained from \(P_{0X,Q}\), the Bernoulli probabilities \(p_{0:T-1,Q}\), Gaussian innovations with variance \(\tau_Q^2\), and the auxiliary standard Gaussian coordinates

symbols.name: P_{N,Q}
symbols.def: the law of the size-\(N\) observed array obtained by drawing primitive rows from \(P_{\xi,Q}\), one independent Gaussian interaction matrix, and applying the homogeneous structural recursion with \((\beta_{0,Q},\sigma_Q^2)\)

symbols.name: \mathbb P_{N,Q}
symbols.def: \(\mathbb P_{N,Q}=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N\delta_{\xi_i}\) when the array is distributed according to \(P_{N,Q}\)

symbols.name: [\cdot]_Q
symbols.def: \([A]_Q\) denotes the displayed generic object \(A\) after replacing \((P_{0X},P_\xi,\beta_0,\sigma^2,\tau^2,p_t,\mathbb P_N)\) by \((P_{0X,Q},P_{\xi,Q},\beta_{0,Q},\sigma_Q^2,\tau_Q^2,p_{t,Q},\mathbb P_{N,Q})\)

symbols.name: f
symbols.role: generic generator of the weak component of the envelope-weighted topology

symbols.name: \mathcal E_T
symbols.role: dominates all displayed row features, test functions, and message derivatives through order three

symbols.name: \mathcal T_{\mathcal E}
symbols.def: the product of the Euclidean topology on \(\vartheta_Q\) and the initial topology on primitive-row laws generated by \(P\mapsto P[f]\) for every bounded continuous test function and by \(P\mapsto P[\mathcal E_T^{2+\delta_{\mathrm{mom}}}]\)

symbols.name: \mathcal Q_T
symbols.role: the typed all-active homogeneous Causal-MP family defined in \(\text{def:model-class}\)

symbols.name: \mathcal K
symbols.role: a compact family carrying the named common constants in \(\text{def:compact-regular-family}\)

symbols.name: d_{\mathrm{BL}}
symbols.role: metric for uniform weak convergence of the fixed-dimensional and finite-index Gaussian laws

assumptions.condition: \(T\) is fixed as \(N\to\infty\).
The entries \(G_{ij}\) are independent \(\mathcal N(0,1)\) variables, and the same matrix is reused for every \(t\).

standard.name: Gaussian dense interactions with time reuse

assumptions.condition: The variables \(W_{i,t+1}\) are independent Bernoulli variables with known probabilities satisfying \(\eta\le p_t\le1-\eta\).
The variables \(\epsilon_{it}\) are independent \(\mathcal N(0,\tau^2)\) variables.
The arrays \(G\), \(W\), \(\epsilon\), and the initial rows \((Y_{i0},X_i)\) are mutually independent.
The rows \((Y_{i0},X_i)\) are independent and identically distributed with law \(P_{0X}\).

standard.name: Independent and identically distributed initial rows

assumptions.condition: The law \(P_{0X}\) has every finite moment required by the derivative envelopes.

Near \(\beta_0\), the map \(g_\beta\) is three times continuously differentiable in its continuous arguments and parameter, with derivatives dominated by integrable polynomial envelopes under the fixed-\(T\) law.
On \(\mathcal B\), the population mean-moment criterion has the unique zero \(\beta_0\).
The Jacobian \(J\) has full column rank.
The matrix \(X_v\) has rank two.
The finite recursion \(\Psi_T\) is Hadamard differentiable at \((\beta_0,\sigma^2,\tau^2,P_{0X})\) tangentially to the initial-row empirical-process directions.
For every \(1\le t<T\), \(\lambda_{\min}\{K_{D_t^{\star}D_t^{\star}}(P)\}>\underline\kappa\).

standard.name: Uniform nonsingularity of finite Gram blocks

assumptions.condition: For every \(0\le t<T\), \(\rho_t(P)>\underline\rho\).
The primitive row law satisfies \(P_\xi\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{rr}}\).
The set \(\mathcal K\) is compact in \(\mathcal T_{\mathcal E}\).

standard.name: Compact uniformity set in a weighted weak topology

assumptions.condition: For every \(Q\in\mathcal K\), one common \(\mathcal E_T\) dominates in absolute value every coordinate of \([\phi_T(\xi;P_\xi)]_Q\), \([I_T(\xi)]_Q\), \([\zeta_T(\xi)]_Q\), and \([\psi_{\theta,T}(\xi)]_Q\), every test function in \(\mathcal F_{0X,T}\), and every message derivative through total order three appearing in \(\mathfrak R_T\), \(\dot{\mathfrak R}_T\), \(\Psi_T\), or \(D\Psi_T\).
\(\sup_{Q\in\mathcal K}P_{\xi,Q}[\mathcal E_T^{2+\delta_{\mathrm{mom}}}]\le B_{\mathcal E}\).
\(\inf_{Q\in\mathcal K}\operatorname{dist}(\beta_{0,Q},\partial\mathcal B)\ge\varepsilon_{\mathcal B}\).

standard.name: Uniform interiority of a finite-dimensional parameter

assumptions.condition: \(\inf_{Q\in\mathcal K}\inf_{\beta\in\mathcal B:\|\beta-\beta_{0,Q}\|\ge\varepsilon_{\mathrm{id}}}\|\mathfrak r_Q(\beta)\|\ge c_{\mathrm{id}}\).
\(\inf_{Q\in\mathcal K}s_{\min}([J]_Q)\ge\underline j\).
\(\inf_{Q\in\mathcal K}s_{\min}([X_v]_Q)\ge\underline x\).
\(\inf_{Q\in\mathcal K}\min_{0\le t<T}\min\{p_{t,Q},1-p_{t,Q}\}\ge\eta\).
\(\inf_{Q\in\mathcal K}\min_{1\le t<T}\lambda_{\min}([K_{D_t^{\star}D_t^{\star}}]_Q)\ge2\underline\kappa\).

standard.name: Uniform nonsingularity of finite Gram blocks

assumptions.condition: \(\inf_{Q\in\mathcal K}\min_{0\le t<T}[\rho_t]_Q\ge2\underline\rho\).

definitions.name: All-active full-rank row-law interior \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{rr}}\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{rr}}=\{P:\lambda_{\min}\{K_{D_t^{\star}D_t^{\star}}(P)\}>\underline\kappa\text{ for every }1\le t<T,\text{ and }\rho_t(P)>\underline\rho\text{ for every }0\le t<T\}\), where \(D_t^{\star}=\{0,\ldots,t-1\}\).

definitions.name: Envelope-weighted weak model-index topology \(\mathcal T_{\mathcal E}\)
definitions.construction: On primitive-row laws, take the initial topology generated by the maps \(P\mapsto P[f]\) for every bounded continuous test function and the moment map \(P\mapsto P[\mathcal E_T^{2+\delta_{\mathrm{mom}}}]\). Thus convergence is ordinary weak convergence plus convergence of the common envelope moment. Equip \(\vartheta_Q=(\beta_{0,Q},\sigma_Q^2,\tau_Q^2,p_{0:T-1,Q})\) with its Euclidean topology. Their product is \(\mathcal T_{\mathcal E}\).

definitions.name: Typed regular model-index family \(\mathcal Q_T\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal Q_T=\{Q=(P_{0X,Q},\vartheta_Q):Q\text{ induces }P_{\xi,Q}\text{ and }(P_{N,Q})_{N\ge1},\text{ and the induced generic objects satisfy }\text{ass:fixed-horizon},\text{ass:gaussian-interactions},\text{ass:bernoulli-design},\text{ass:gaussian-innovations},\text{ass:primitive-independence},\text{ass:initial-iid},\text{ass:initial-moments},\text{ass:smooth-messages},\text{ass:identified-branch},\text{ass:mean-rank},\text{ass:variance-excitation},\text{ass:path-smoothness},\text{ and }P_{\xi,Q}\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{rr}}\}\). Each \(Q\) therefore determines both a primitive-row law and a finite-\(N\) array law, rather than identifying a row law with an array-law sequence.

definitions.name: Admissible compact regular family \(\mathcal K\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal K\) is any subset of \(\mathcal Q_T\) satisfying \(\text{ass:family-compactness}\), \(\text{ass:uniform-envelope}\), \(\text{ass:uniform-envelope-moment}\), \(\text{ass:uniform-chart-interior}\), \(\text{ass:uniform-identification}\), \(\text{ass:uniform-mean-rank}\), \(\text{ass:uniform-variance-rank}\), \(\text{ass:uniform-overlap}\), \(\text{ass:uniform-gram-margin}\), and \(\text{ass:uniform-residual-margin}\), with the same named constants \(\delta_{\mathrm{mom}},B_{\mathcal E},\varepsilon_{\mathcal B},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{id}},c_{\mathrm{id}},\underline j,\underline x,\eta,\underline\kappa,\underline\rho\) for every \(Q\in\mathcal K\).

definitions.name: All-active Gaussian conditioning recursion
definitions.construction: For \(P\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{rr}}\), use \(D_t^{\star}=\{0,\ldots,t-1\}\), compute \(\lambda_t(P)\) and \(\rho_t(P)\), and generate \(H_{it}=\lambda_t(P)^{\top}H_{i,D_t^{\star}}+\sqrt{\rho_t(P)}Z_{it}^{\circ}\) for every \(0\le t<T\). The strict inequalities defining \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{rr}}\) make every inverse and square-root derivative ordinary on an open neighborhood. Iterating these operations gives \(\mathfrak R_T(P)\).

definitions.name: Finite-\(N\) all-active Gaussian bridge recursion
definitions.construction: At date \(t\), condition on \(\mathscr F_{N,t}\), compute the observable empirical coefficients \(\lambda_t^{N}=(K_{D_t^{\star}D_t^{\star}}^{N})^{-1}K_{D_t^{\star},t}^{N}\) and \(\rho_t^{N}=K_{tt}^{N}-K_{t,D_t^{\star}}^{N}(K_{D_t^{\star}D_t^{\star}}^{N})^{-1}K_{D_t^{\star},t}^{N}\), and form \(H_{it}^{\circ,N}=(\lambda_t^{N})^{\top}H_{i,D_t^{\star}}^{\circ,N}+\sqrt{\rho_t^{N}}Z_{it}^{\circ}\). Iterate sequentially while \(\mathcal A_{N,t}^{\mathrm{act}}\) holds, recomputing messages and empirical Gram coefficients from the generated past after each update, and stop at the first exit from the all-active domain.

definitions.name: Ordered empirical moment vector
definitions.construction: On \(\{\mathbb P_N\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{rr}}\}\), compute the all-active full-rank recursion \(\mathfrak R_T(\mathbb P_N)\), evaluate \(\phi_T(\xi;\mathbb P_N)\), and set \(M_N=\mathbb P_N[\phi_T(\xi;\mathbb P_N)]\); set \(M_N=0\) otherwise. Set \(M_T=P_\xi[\phi_T(\xi;P_\xi)]\).

definitions.name: All-active projection differentiation handle
definitions.construction: For an admissible compact family \(\mathcal K\), evaluate each \(Q\)-specific recursion on \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{rr}}\), differentiate the full-past projection and every positive square-root residual along an arbitrary ambient empirical-process direction \(h\) satisfying \(h[1]=0\), and apply \([\dot{\mathfrak R}_T[h]]_Q\) coordinatewise to \(\phi_T\). The handle is a uniform von Mises expansion using the common envelope bound \((\delta_{\mathrm{mom}},B_{\mathcal E})\), chart and identification margins \((\varepsilon_{\mathcal B},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{id}},c_{\mathrm{id}})\), rank bounds \((\underline j,\underline x)\), overlap \(\eta\), and interior margins \((\underline\kappa,\underline\rho)\) to control every row-averaged second-order remainder.

definitions.name: Homogeneous fluctuation state evolution
definitions.construction: For each primitive row \(\xi\), evaluate \(\dot{\mathfrak R}_T[\delta_\xi-P_\xi]\) by ordinary differentiation on the open all-active domain \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{rr}}\), then evaluate \(I_T(\xi)=\phi_T(\xi;P_\xi)-M_T+P_\xi[\dot\phi_T(\widetilde\xi;P_\xi)[\delta_\xi-P_\xi]]\) and set \(\Gamma_T=P_\xi[I_T(\xi)I_T(\xi)^{\top}]\). Augment this moment influence with \(f(Y_0,X)-P_{0X}f\), for \(f\in\mathcal F_{0X,T}\), to obtain the single Gaussian experiment \(\mathbb Z_T^{\mathrm{full}}\); its displayed covariance formula supplies all moment, initial empirical-process, and cross-block covariances. For \(Q\in\mathcal K\), brackets \([\cdot]_Q\) evaluate this same recursion and covariance at the model index; no separately sampled Gaussian or initial-law object is introduced.

definitions.name: Observable structural estimator
definitions.construction: Compute \(\widehat\beta\) from \(r_N\), compute \(\widehat q\) and \(\widehat X_v\), set \((\widehat\sigma^2,\widehat\tau^2)^{\top}=(\widehat X_v^{\top}W_v\widehat X_v)^{-1}\widehat X_v^{\top}W_v\widehat v\), and compute \(\widehat K\).

definitions.name: Full-initial-law counterfactual path
definitions.construction: Use the displayed \(\Psi_T\): integrate the first message and its square under the joint law \(P_{0X}\), then, only after the first dense interaction, integrate each later message under \(P_X\) and an independent Gaussian state with recursively updated mean and variance; take \(\theta_T=(m_t^{(1)}-m_t^{(0)})_{t=1}^T\).

definitions.name: Feasible unstudentized Gaussian-max path band
definitions.construction: Compute \(\widehat\zeta_i\) as the observable plug-in counterpart of the population row influence \(\zeta_T(\xi_i)\), apply the same forward derivative \(D\Psi_T\) to obtain \(\widehat\psi_{\theta,T,i}\), and set \(\widehat\Omega_\theta=N^{-1}\sum_i\widehat\psi_{\theta,T,i}\widehat\psi_{\theta,T,i}^{\top}\), targeting exactly \(\Omega_\theta=P_\xi[\psi_{\theta,T}(\xi)\psi_{\theta,T}(\xi)^{\top}]\). Draw \(Z^\theta\mid\text{data}\sim\mathcal N(0,\widehat\Omega_\theta)\), take the conditional \(1-\alpha\) quantile of \(\max_{1\le t\le T}|Z_t^\theta|\), and report \(\mathcal C_N\) without estimating an active set or dividing by a variance.

definitions.name: Redundant-message rank-boundary diagnostic
definitions.construction: Take \(K_{00}>0\) and choose \(V_i\in L_2(P_\xi)\) with \(P_\xi[U_{i0}V_i]=0\) and \(P_\xi[V_i^2]=1\). Set \(U_{i1}^{(\delta)}=U_{i0}+\delta V_i\). Projection on \(U_{i0}\) gives coefficient one, residual energy \(\rho_1=\delta^2\), and conditioned field \(H_{i1}=H_{i0}+|\delta|Z_{i1}^{\circ}\).

statements.statement: Fix \(N\), \(T\), and \(0\le t<T\). On \(\mathcal A_{N,t}^{\mathrm{act}}\), Gaussian row conditioning gives the exact regular conditional law \[\mathcal L\!\left((H_{it}^{G,N})_{i=1}^N\mid\mathscr F_{N,t}\right)=\mathcal L\!\left(\left((\lambda_t^{N})^{\top}H_{i,D_t^{\star}}^{G,N}+\sqrt{\rho_t^{N}}Z_{it}^{\circ}\right)_{i=1}^N\mid\mathscr F_{N,t}\right).\] Conditionally on \(\mathscr F_{N,t}\), the \(Z_{it}^{\circ}\) are independent standard Gaussians, \(\lambda_t^{N}=(K_{D_t^{\star}D_t^{\star}}^{N})^{-1}K_{D_t^{\star},t}^{N}\), and \(\rho_t^{N}=K_{tt}^{N}-K_{t,D_t^{\star}}^{N}(K_{D_t^{\star}D_t^{\star}}^{N})^{-1}K_{D_t^{\star},t}^{N}\). Iterating these kernels through \(t=0,\ldots,T-1\), stopping at the first exit from the all-active domain, yields conditional equality in law between the stopped observed reused-\(G\) field--outcome--message path and the stopped auxiliary path in \(\text{def:finite-n-bridge-recursion}\). On the event of no exit, the equality holds jointly for the complete paths and every displayed measurable statistic, including \(M_N\), \(r_N\), \(\widehat v\), message Gram products, and mean- and variance-score moments.
statements.justification: This fixed-sample bridge is the exact probabilistic link from the observed reused matrix to the auxiliary recursion differentiated in the CFSE.
statements.gap: Bayati and Montanari provide adaptive Gaussian conditioning for AMP with an Onsager correction, whereas this finite-\(N\), full-past equality in law with empirical Gram coefficients is not stated for the non-Onsager Causal-MP recursion.
statements.consumer: The public CausalMP implementation can use the recursion as an exact conditional simulator and covariance-engine primitive.

statements.statement: For every admissible compact family \(\mathcal K\), \(\sup_{Q\in\mathcal K}P_{N,Q}\{\mathbb P_{N,Q}\notin\mathcal U_{\mathrm{rr}}\}\to0\). Consequently, uniformly over \(Q\in\mathcal K\), the empirical moment vector is computed by the same all-active full-rank recursion with probability tending to one; every \(K_{D_t^{\star}D_t^{\star}}^{N}\) has smallest eigenvalue exceeding \(\underline\kappa\), and every \(\rho_t^{N}\) exceeds \(\underline\rho\).
statements.justification: This interior-stability result makes the observable empirical statistic use the same full-rank recursion as its population limit.
statements.gap: Standard laws of large numbers do not by themselves record stability of every recursively generated Gram inverse and Schur residual in this adaptive reused-matrix system.
statements.consumer: The covariance implementation may run the ordinary full-rank derivative recursion without data-dependent deletion on events whose probability tends to one.

statements.statement: For every admissible compact family \(\mathcal K\), does ordinary differentiation of the all-active recursion along ambient empirical-process directions yield, uniformly over \(Q\in\mathcal K\), \[\sqrt N\{[M_N]_Q-[M_T]_Q\}=N^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^N[I_T(\xi_i)]_Q+o_{P_{N,Q}}(1),\] jointly with \(\sqrt N([\widehat P_{0X}]_Q-P_{0X,Q})\) on \(\mathcal F_{0X,T}\), while every row-averaged Taylor remainder for messages, Gram products, mean-score coordinates, and variance-score coordinates is \(o_{P_{N,Q}}(N^{-1/2})\) on \(\{\mathbb P_{N,Q}\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{rr}}\}\)?
statements.justification: This is the genuine proof boundary on a full-rank open neighborhood; no central limit theorem is assumed.
statements.gap: First-order state evolution, concentration, and entrywise leave-one-out theory do not establish this aggregate root-\(N\) expansion for a reused-matrix causal recursion.
statements.consumer: A positive answer yields analytic inference for every fixed-dimensional smooth Causal-MP moment configuration.

statements.statement: For every admissible compact family \(\mathcal K\), \(\sup_{Q\in\mathcal K}P_{N,Q}\{\mathbb P_{N,Q}\notin\mathcal U_{\mathrm{rr}}\}\to0\), and \[\sup_{Q\in\mathcal K}d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left(\mathcal L_{P_{N,Q}}\!\left(\sqrt N\{[M_N]_Q-[M_T]_Q\},\sqrt N\{[\widehat P_{0X}]_Q-P_{0X,Q}\}\right),\mathcal L\{[\mathbb Z_T^{\mathrm{full}}]_Q\}\right)\to0\] in \(\mathbb R^{\dim(M_T)}\times\ell^\infty(\mathcal F_{0X,T})\). At each \(Q\), the covariance is the single bilinear formula defining \([\mathbb Z_T^{\mathrm{full}}]_Q\); hence \(\operatorname{Var}([Z_M]_Q)=[\Gamma_T]_Q\), including every cross-covariance between the initial empirical-process block and the reused-matrix mean, energy, Gram, and score blocks.
statements.justification: The joint fluctuation law is the missing inferential layer between state evolution and causal-path uncertainty.
statements.gap: Shirani and Bayati establish first-order state evolution and consistency, while available AMP results do not give this aggregate covariance recursion.
statements.consumer: Configured Causal-MP regressions can replace an independence-based sandwich matrix by \(\Gamma_T\).

statements.statement: For every admissible compact family \(\mathcal K\), uniformly over \(Q\in\mathcal K\), the \(Q\)-evaluations of \(r_N(\beta_0)\) and \(\widehat v-\sigma^2(N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^NU_{it}^2)_{t=0}^{T-1}-\tau^2\mathbf 1_T\) have a joint centered Gaussian root-\(N\) limit with covariance \([\operatorname{blockdiag}\{C,2(C\circ C)\}]_Q\) and zero mixed block.
statements.justification: This cancellation turns the general CFSE into closed observable residual blocks.
statements.gap: No cited Causal-MP or AMP result states this block identity for one reused nonsymmetric latent matrix.
statements.consumer: It supplies standard errors for the unpenalized full-population \(\texttt{CFEEstimator}\) configuration.

statements.statement: For every admissible compact family \(\mathcal K\), the bounded-Lipschitz distance, uniformly over \(Q\in\mathcal K\), between the \(P_{N,Q}\)-law of \[\sqrt N\left([\widehat\beta-\beta_0]_Q,[\widehat\sigma^2-\sigma^2]_Q,[\widehat\tau^2-\tau^2]_Q,[\widehat P_{0X}]_Q-P_{0X,Q}\right)\] and the law of \([\mathcal A_T\mathbb Z_T^{\mathrm{full}}]_Q=([LZ_m]_Q,[A_v\{Z_v-\sigma^2Q_\beta LZ_m\}]_Q,[\mathbb G_{0X}]_Q)\) on \(\mathcal F_{0X,T}\) tends to zero.
statements.justification: This law propagates same-panel residual dependence to every fitted input of the counterfactual recursion.
statements.gap: Causal-MP gives consistency, not the same-sample variance-score correction in this expansion.
statements.consumer: The public estimator obtains a joint covariance for its fitted structural inputs.

statements.statement: For every admissible compact family \(\mathcal K\) and every \(\varepsilon>0\), \[\sup_{Q\in\mathcal K}P_{N,Q}\!\left(\left\|\sqrt N[\widehat\theta_T-\theta_T]_Q-N^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^N[\psi_{\theta,T}(\xi_i)]_Q\right\|>\varepsilon\right)\to0.\] The limiting vector is \([D\Psi_T(\beta_0,\sigma^2,\tau^2,P_{0X})[\mathcal A_T\mathbb Z_T^{\mathrm{full}}]]_Q\sim\mathcal N(0,[\Omega_\theta]_Q)\). The observable covariance estimator is uniformly consistent for exactly this influence covariance: for every \(\varepsilon>0\), \(\sup_{Q\in\mathcal K}P_{N,Q}(\|[\widehat\Omega_\theta-\Omega_\theta]_Q\|>\varepsilon)\to0\). Consequently, \[\liminf_{N\to\infty}\inf_{Q\in\mathcal K}P_{N,Q}\{[\theta_{T,t}]_Q\in[\mathcal C_{N,t}]_Q\text{ for every }1\le t\le T\}\ge1-\alpha.\] Equality holds pointwise at any \(Q\) for which the maximum absolute coordinate of \(\mathcal N(0,[\Omega_\theta]_Q)\) has a continuous nondegenerate distribution.
statements.justification: The band supports simultaneous claims about the entire dynamic treatment-effect path without an unobservable active-coordinate set.
statements.gap: The published Causal-MP confidence-interval discussion is heuristic, while generic Gaussian-max theory does not derive the common-disorder and nuisance influence terms.
statements.consumer: The one-batch, zero-ridge \(\texttt{CFEEstimator}\) can return analytic simultaneous path bands, including at zero-variance coordinates.

statements.statement: In \(\text{def:affine-witness}\), the observed recursion \(Y_{i,t+1}=\overline U_t+H_{it}^{G,N}+\epsilon_{it}\), \(U_{it}=Y_{it}/2+W_{i,t+1}\), gives the checked table \[\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c}t&\mathbb E[Y_t]&\mathbb E[Y_t^2]&\mathbb E[U_t]&q_t=\mathbb E[U_t^2]\\\hline 0&0&1&1/4&1/4+p_0=1/2\\1&1/4&25/16&7/8&25/64+p_1(1/4)+p_1=85/64\\2&7/8&99/32&11/16&99/128+p_2(7/8)+p_2=159/128\end{array}\] using \(\mathbb E[(Y_t/2+W_{t+1})^2]=\mathbb E[Y_t^2]/4+p_t\mathbb E[Y_t]+p_t\), including the Bernoulli cross term \(\mathbb E[Y_tW_{t+1}]=p_t\mathbb E[Y_t]\). The relevant Gram entry and variance-design determinant are \[K_{01}=\tfrac12\mathbb E[U_0Y_1]+p_1\mathbb E[U_0]=1/32+3/16=7/32,\qquad \det(X_v^{\top}X_v)=3\sum_{t=0}^2q_t^2-\left(\sum_{t=0}^2q_t\right)^2=10191/8192.\] Furthermore, \(\Delta_{1,N}^{Y}=\sqrt N(\overline U_0-1/4)+A_{0,N}^{G}+\sqrt N\,\overline\epsilon_0\) has limiting variance \(7/16+1/2+1=31/16\), while \(\Delta_{2,N}^{Y}=\tfrac12\Delta_{1,N}^{Y}+\sqrt N(\overline W_2-3/4)+A_{1,N}^{G}+\sqrt N\,\overline\epsilon_1\). The sole same-matrix-reuse contribution is \(\lim_N\operatorname{Cov}(\Delta_{1,N}^{Y},A_{1,N}^{G})=K_{01}=7/32\), so \(\lim_N\operatorname{Cov}(\Delta_{1,N}^{Y},\Delta_{2,N}^{Y})=(1/2)(31/16)+7/32=19/16\). The residual blocks are \(C\), \(2(C\circ C)\), and zero mixed covariance. For the counterfactual recursion, \(\mu_0^{(a)}=a\), \(\kappa_0^{(a)}=1/4+a^2\), \((m_1^{(a)},m_2^{(a)},m_3^{(a)})=(a,3a/2,7a/4)\), and \(\theta_3=(1,3/2,7/4)\).
statements.justification: This recomputed special case verifies both the energy arithmetic and the corrected first-step use of the full initial law.
statements.gap: Published Causal-MP examples do not report this reuse covariance, determinant, or counterfactual-path reduction.
statements.consumer: The identities form a deterministic regression test for the covariance and path implementations.

sampling_model.units: For each \(Q\in\mathcal Q_T\), independent and identically distributed primitive rows with law \(P_{\xi,Q}\) and one latent dense Gaussian interaction matrix induce the finite-array law \(P_{N,Q}\) over a fixed horizon.
sampling_model.treatment: Randomized independently across units and dates and entering \(g_{\beta_0}\).
sampling_model.overlap: The fixed constant \(\eta>0\) bounds all assignment probabilities.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate \(\beta_0\) from mean moments, \(\sigma^2\) and \(\tau^2\) from the energy regression, the full \(K\) from fitted messages, and the initial law by its empirical distribution. Uniform claims range only over admissible compact \(\mathcal K\) with the common constants in \(\text{def:compact-regular-family}\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The published article's Theorems 1--2 in Section 3 establish first-order state evolution and consistency, while Section 2.5 describes confidence-interval analysis as heuristic.
Theorem 1 establishes fixed-iteration AMP state evolution using adaptive Gaussian conditioning.
Theorem 1 gives exponential finite-sample concentration of pseudo-Lipschitz AMP observables.
The article gives nonasymptotic leave-one-out representations and state-evolution control for AMP iterates.
The article develops simultaneous causal inference for multiple derived outcomes in a hierarchical setting.
The paper establishes Gaussian and conditional multiplier approximations for maxima of sums of independent random vectors.
The paper establishes first-order AMP universality through tensor-network arguments.

The NeurIPS 2024 paper learns state-evolution update functions from mean, variance, treatment, and nonlinear higher-order features and reports empirical interval or error-bar behavior, but does not prove an analytic root-\(N\) joint covariance, feasible influence covariance, or simultaneous coverage law.

tldr: A fixed-horizon randomized experiment under homogeneous Causal-MP has a root-\(N\) fluctuation state evolution even though one unobserved Gaussian interaction matrix is reused at every date. An exact finite-\(N\) bridge conditions on the full observed past and uses empirical Gram projections to couple the reused-matrix fields to the auxiliary Gaussian-residual recursion. The theorem is uniform over an explicitly typed compact family \(\mathcal K\subset\mathcal Q_T\) under named common moment, identification, rank, overlap, Gram, and Schur-residual margins. A single joint Gaussian experiment combines the differentiated mean, energy, Gram, and score moments with the initial-row empirical process. Its structural loading gives a direct asymptotic-linear representation for the all-treated-minus-none-treated path, and observable row contributions estimate the same covariance used by simultaneous Gaussian-max bands.

project_justification.gap: Causal-MP supplies first-order state evolution, consistent total-treatment-effect estimation, and heuristic intervals, but no root-\(N\) law for empirical means, second moments, or scores under reuse of one latent matrix.
project_justification.niche: Order-\(N^{-1/2}\) common-disorder terms are discarded by first-order laws and cannot be recovered by treating panel rows as independent.
project_justification.fill: Establish the finite-\(N\) conditional bridge with empirical Gram coefficients, construct the ordered auxiliary recursion and its ordinary derivative on the all-active interior, prove the expansion uniformly on compact \(\mathcal K\subset\mathcal Q_T\), derive one joint moment--initial-law Gaussian experiment, map it through the structural and counterfactual derivatives, and calibrate an observable simultaneous path band from plug-in estimates of the same row influence.

related_work: Shirani and Bayati (2024, published Section 3, Theorems 1--2) establish first-order state evolution and consistency; their published Section 2.5 labels confidence-interval analysis heuristic. Bayati, Luo, Overman, Shirani, and Xiong (2024, Sections 2--4 and Algorithm 1) learn higher-order state-evolution update functions from observed mean, variance, treatment, and nonlinear features and discuss empirical intervals or replicated error bars, but they do not prove the proposed analytic root-\(N\) joint covariance, feasible influence covariance, or simultaneous coverage law. Bayati and Montanari (2011) supply adaptive Gaussian conditioning for AMP with an Onsager correction; the relevant distinction is the exact finite-\(N\) full-past bridge with empirical Gram coefficients for a reused nonsymmetric matrix and no Onsager correction. Rush and Venkataramanan (2018) establish finite-sample concentration, and Bao, Han, and Xu (2025) establish leave-one-out representations; these papers inform the projection and remainder arguments without claiming the aggregate causal fluctuation law. Qiu, Sun, and Zhou (2024) study multiple derived causal outcomes, while Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2013) supply Gaussian-max calibration after asymptotic linearity. Wang, Zhong, and Fan (2024) and Gueddari, Hachem, and Najim (2025) concern broader first-order AMP laws rather than centered Causal-MP covariance.
technical_internal_limitation: The target is the deterministic population-limit path, not a realized finite-network counterfactual path. The theory is fixed-\(T\), Gaussian-interaction, and confined to compact regular families \(\mathcal K\subset\mathcal Q_T\) with the named common envelope, chart, identification, rank, overlap, Gram, and Schur-residual constants in \(\text{def:compact-regular-family}\). Rank-changing laws and exact zero-pivot laws are excluded boundary cases; no continuity or differentiability is claimed there. In \(\text{def:rank-boundary-perturbation}\), \(U_{i1}^{(\delta)}=U_{i0}+\delta V_i\) gives residual energy \(\delta^2\) and field \(H_{i0}+|\delta|Z_{i1}^{\circ}\), so the two-sided derivative fails at the redundant-message boundary. Weak energy designs, variance boundaries, fixed positive ridge, model selection, and growing horizons require separate limits.
honest_scope: The finite-\(N\) Gaussian bridge uses the conditioning fields \(\mathscr F_{N,t}\) and empirical coefficients \(K^N,\lambda_t^N,\rho_t^N\); the open content is the uniformly root-\(N\) row-averaged linearization on each admissible compact \(\mathcal K\subset\mathcal Q_T\), where \(Q\) induces both \(P_{\xi,Q}\) and \(P_{N,Q}\). The topology \(\mathcal T_{\mathcal E}\) combines envelope-weighted weak convergence of primitive-row laws with Euclidean convergence of finite-dimensional parameters. The common constants \(\delta_{\mathrm{mom}},B_{\mathcal E},\varepsilon_{\mathcal B},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{id}},c_{\mathrm{id}},\underline j,\underline x,\eta,\underline\kappa,\underline\rho\) control moments, chart distance, identification, the two rank conditions, overlap, Gram blocks, and Schur residuals. The empirical law remains in the same all-active open neighborhood uniformly, and derivatives use the ordinary ambient empirical-process tangent space. Rank-changing and exact zero-pivot laws remain outside the theorem. The single experiment \(\mathbb Z_T^{\mathrm{full}}\) contains the complete moment vector and initial-row empirical process; the path influence is \(D\Psi_T[\zeta_T(\xi)]\), so \(\Omega_\theta\) and \(\widehat\Omega_\theta\) refer to the same row-level object. The counterfactual first transition integrates under \(P_{0X}\), and Gaussian integration begins only after the dense interaction creates the Gaussian state. In the affine \(T=3\) reduction, the checked table gives \(q=(1/2,85/64,159/128)\), \(K_{01}=7/32\), \(\det(X_v^{\top}X_v)=10191/8192\), consecutive mean covariance \(19/16\), reuse component \(7/32\), and causal path \((1,3/2,7/4)\). At \(T=1\), the influence recursion reduces to the ordinary empirical initial-row fluctuation plus the Gaussian structural residual.
novelty_justification: The closest published causal results establish first-order state evolution and consistency or learn higher-order state-evolution features with empirical interval displays. Neither supplies an exact finite-\(N\) reused-matrix bridge tied to an analytic aggregate influence recursion, a joint root-\(N\) covariance including the initial-law cross block, a feasible covariance for the same path influence, or a simultaneous coverage law. The kernel conditions with empirical full-past Gram coefficients before differentiating the population recursion, retains same-matrix reuse terms, yields \(\operatorname{blockdiag}\{C,2(C\circ C)\}\), and propagates the observable law through structural and counterfactual recursions. The checked affine covariance \(19/16\), including reuse contribution \(7/32\), separates the claim from first-order state evolution.
message: Specified the exact fixed-\(N\) Gaussian bridge with conditioning sigma-fields and empirical Gram coefficients, propagated it through CFSE and path inference, and supplied the complete checked \(T=3\) affine moment and covariance table.
